# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Duong_2026_cobimetinib"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Duong_2026_cobimetinib"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70282>

Duong 2026 is a proof-of-principle simulation study. A representative patient
takes cobimetinib 60 mg once daily on a 21-days-on / 7-days-off (21/7)
schedule. Deterministic one-compartment plasma PK supplies a free plasma
concentration that is identical for every tumour cell. Each cell takes the
drug up at a rate proportional to its own influx-transporter count `T_i`
(log-normal across cells), clears it by first-order intracellular metabolism,
and accumulates a death hazard through a sigmoid-Emax function of its
intracellular concentration. A cell dies when its cumulative hazard reaches
`-log(U_i)` with `U_i ~ Uniform(0, 1)`; the population goes extinct when the
last cell dies.

In the packaged model **one simulated subject is one tumour cell**. The
per-cell random effect `etalkin_int_tumor` carries the transporter
heterogeneity: `T_i = 500 * exp(etalkin_int_tumor)`, so the uptake rate
constant `k_in * T_i` is log-normal with geometric mean `0.038 * 500 = 19`
1/h and log-scale SD 0.5. The model returns the cell's cumulative hazard
`cumhaz` and survival probability `sur = exp(-cumhaz)`. Drawing `U_i` and
taking the maximum death time over a population of cells is done outside the
model, as in the authors' code, and is shown below.

# Population

No patient data were fitted. All parameter values are literature-derived or
calibrated (Methods, Parameter Justification). The systemic PK represents one
typical patient; the cellular layer represents a tumour of `N` cells
(`N = 100` in Experiment 2, `N = 100` to `2000` in Experiment 4) whose
transporter counts are drawn from `LogNormal(log(500), 0.5^2)` (a coefficient of
variation of 53%).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Duong_2026_cobimetinib")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Duong_2026_cobimetinib.R`. The authors'
Julia code (supplementary `pk.jl`, `cellular_dynamics.jl`, `models.jl`) was
read alongside the text to confirm structure and units.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| One-compartment first-order absorption PK, superposition of doses | -- | Methods, Systemic Pharmacokinetics; `pk.jl` |
| `lka` (ka) | 2.0 1/h | Methods, Systemic Pharmacokinetics |
| `lvc` (V/F) | 806 L | Methods, Systemic Pharmacokinetics |
| `lkel` (ke) | 0.0171 1/h | Methods, Systemic Pharmacokinetics |
| `fu`, `Cu = fu * Cc` | 0.05 | Methods, Systemic Pharmacokinetics |
| `dC_i = (k_in T_i C_p,u - k_met C_i) dt + sigma_C dW_i` | -- | Methods, Cellular Pharmacokinetics; `cellular_dynamics.jl` `euler_maruyama_step!` |
| `lkin_int_tumor` (k_in x median T) | 0.038 1/h x 500 = 19 1/h | Methods, Cellular Pharmacokinetics (`k_in = 0.038`, `mu_T = log 500`) |
| `lkout_int_tumor` (k_met) | 0.1 1/h | Methods, Cellular Pharmacokinetics |
| `etalkin_int_tumor` (sigma_T^2) | 0.5^2 = 0.25 | Methods, Cellular Pharmacokinetics (`sigma_T = 0.5`) |
| `mu_i = mu_max C_i^n / (EC50^n + C_i^n)` | -- | Methods, Cellular Pharmacodynamics and Death Process |
| `lemax` (mu_max) | 1.5 1/day | Methods, Cellular Pharmacodynamics |
| `lec50` (EC50) | 2.0 | Methods, Cellular Pharmacodynamics |
| `lhill` (n) | 2.5 | Methods, Cellular Pharmacodynamics |
| `H_i(t) = integral of mu_i`, death at `H_i >= -log(U_i)` | -- | Methods, Cellular Pharmacodynamics; `cellular_dynamics.jl` `update_hazard!`, `check_death!` |
| sigma_C (omitted) | 0.01 | Methods, Cellular Pharmacokinetics |

# Simulation set-up

Dosing follows the 21/7 schedule for 180 days. The plasma PK is solved with
the cell layer for a grid of 161 transporter counts spanning `+/- 5` log-scale
SDs around the median, each grid point being one subject with its
`etalkin_int_tumor` set explicitly. Because the cellular ODE is linear in
`T_i` and starts from zero, a cell's state is a smooth function of `T_i`; the
extinction-time Monte Carlo below interpolates between neighbouring grid
cells instead of solving every one of the 10^5 to 10^6 cells it draws.

```{r solve}
mod <- readModelDb("Duong_2026_cobimetinib")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)

sigma_t <- 0.5 # log-scale SD of the transporter count, Methods
dose_days <- unlist(lapply(0:6, function(cycle) cycle * 28 + 0:20))
dose_days <- dose_days[dose_days < 180]
dt <- 0.5
tgrid <- seq(0, 180 * 24, by = dt)

ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 60, time = dose_days * 24, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(tgrid, cmt = "central")

zgrid <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 161)
log_t_grid <- log(500) + sigma_t * zgrid
cells <- data.frame(etalkin_int_tumor = sigma_t * zgrid)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  ui,
  events = ev, params = cells, returnType = "data.frame",
  rtol = 1e-8, atol = 1e-10
)
stopifnot(nrow(sim) == length(tgrid) * nrow(cells))

# One column per grid cell, one row per output time
as_grid <- function(col) matrix(sim[[col]], nrow = length(tgrid))
cumhaz_grid <- as_grid("cumhaz")
hazard_grid <- as_grid("hazard")
conc_grid <- as_grid("int_tumor")
median_cell <- which.min(abs(zgrid))
typ <- sim[sim$sim.id == median_cell, ]
```

The intracellular state scales exactly with `T_i`: the ratio of any cell's
concentration to the median cell's is `T_i / 500` at every time point. This is
a property of the ODE (same drawn parameters on both sides), so the tolerance
is the integration tolerance.

```{r linearity}
ratio <- conc_grid[-1, ] / conc_grid[-1, median_cell]
expected <- matrix(exp(sigma_t * zgrid), nrow = nrow(ratio), ncol = ncol(ratio), byrow = TRUE)
max_rel_err <- max(abs(ratio / expected - 1))
max_rel_err
stopifnot(max_rel_err < 1e-6) # measured ~2e-8
```

# Systemic pharmacokinetics

The paper states that, at steady state, the PK reproduces Tmax = 2.4 h, an
accumulation factor of about 2.9 and a free peak of about 0.01 (Methods,
Systemic Pharmacokinetics). The packaged ODE is first checked against the
paper's closed-form superposition equation, then PKNCA summarises day 1 and
day 9.

```{r pk-closed-form}
closed_form <- function(t) {
  vapply(t, function(tt) {
    s <- tt - dose_days * 24
    s <- s[s >= 0]
    sum(60 / 806 * 2.0 / (2.0 - 0.0171) * (exp(-0.0171 * s) - exp(-2.0 * s)))
  }, numeric(1))
}
chk <- typ[typ$time <= 21 * 24 & typ$time > 0, ]
pk_rel_err <- max(abs(chk$Cc / closed_form(chk$time) - 1))
pk_rel_err
stopifnot(pk_rel_err < 1e-6) # measured ~6e-9
```

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  typ |>
    dplyr::filter(time <= 24) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Day 1", tad = time),
  typ |>
    dplyr::filter(time >= 192, time <= 216) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Day 9", tad = time - 192)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cu)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, tad, Cu)
nca_dose <- data.frame(id = 1L, treatment = c("Day 1", "Day 9"), tad = 0, amt = 60)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cu ~ tad | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ tad | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
nca_wide |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Interval" = treatment, "Free Cmax" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "Free AUC0-24" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "PKNCA on the free plasma concentration, day 1 and day 9.")
```

```{r pk-compare}
reference <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("Day 1", "Day 9"),
  tmax = c(2.4, NA),
  cmax = c(NA, 0.01)
)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_res, reference,
  by = "treatment", params = c("cmax", "tmax"), tolerance_pct = 20
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated vs. stated PK. Reference Tmax is the analytic single-dose value log(ka/ke)/(ka-ke) = 2.4 h that the authors' code checks against; the free Cmax reference is the stated steady-state free peak of about 0.01.")

acc <- nca_wide$cmax[nca_wide$treatment == "Day 9"] / nca_wide$cmax[nca_wide$treatment == "Day 1"]
acc
stopifnot(abs(acc / 2.9 - 1) < 0.05)
```

The day-9 Tmax (about 2 h on the 0.5 h output grid) is earlier than 2.4 h
because drug carried over from earlier doses is already declining when the
next dose is absorbed; the 2.4 h quoted in the paper is the single-dose
analytic value, reproduced on
day 1.

```{r pk-plot, fig.cap = "Typical plasma (free) and median-cell intracellular cobimetinib over the first 56 days of 21/7 dosing."}
typ |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 56 * 24) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    time_day = time / 24,
    `Free plasma (Cu x 100)` = Cu * 100,
    `Median-cell intracellular` = int_tumor
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time_day) |>
  ggplot(aes(time_day, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 2.0, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Concentration", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The dashed line is EC50 = 2.0. The authors calibrated `k_in / k_met = 0.38` so
that the median cell sits near EC50 at the typical steady-state free plasma
level under the quasi-steady-state (QSS) relation `C_i = 0.38 * T_i * C_p,u`;
with the full ODE the median cell peaks somewhat lower because `k_met` smooths
the plasma peaks.

# Amplification factor (Experiment 1, Figure 1, Table S3)

The amplification factor is `A = Var(mu_i) / Var(T_i)` evaluated at day 9,
3 h after the dose, using the QSS concentration `C_i = kappa * T_i * C_p,u`
(Methods, Computational Implementation). It is deterministic given the plasma
level, so it is computed here by quadrature over the log-normal transporter
distribution, using the free plasma concentration from the packaged model.

```{r amplification}
cu_195 <- typ$Cu[typ$time == 195]
kappa <- exp(log(0.038 * 500)) / 500 / 0.1
amp <- function(sigma, n = 2.5, ec50 = 2.0, dose_mult = 1) {
  z <- seq(-8, 8, length.out = 4001)
  w <- dnorm(z) / sum(dnorm(z))
  t_i <- 500 * exp(sigma * z)
  c_i <- kappa * t_i * cu_195 * dose_mult
  mu <- 1.5 * c_i^n / (ec50^n + c_i^n)
  var_mu <- sum(w * mu^2) - sum(w * mu)^2
  var_t <- sum(w * t_i^2) - sum(w * t_i)^2
  var_mu / var_t
}
a_base <- amp(sigma_t)
a_base
# Paper: A = 1.525e-6 +/- 1.47e-8 (Results, Extended Observation); Table S2c
# replicate means 1.445e-6 to 1.536e-6 across population sizes.
stopifnot(abs(a_base / 1.525e-6 - 1) < 0.1)
```

# Extinction-time distributions (Experiment 2, Table 1, Figure 2)

Each population has `N = 100` cells, observed for 56 days (two 21/7 cycles);
1000 populations per model variant, as in the paper. A cell's death time is
the first output time at which its cumulative hazard reaches `-log(U_i)`. For a
cell between two grid transporter counts, the death times of the neighbouring
grid cells are found from their own cumulative-hazard curves and interpolated
linearly in `log(T)`.

```{r death-time}
death_times <- function(log_t, threshold, window) {
  keep <- tgrid <= window
  tt <- tgrid[keep]
  j <- pmin(pmax(findInterval(log_t, log_t_grid), 1L), length(log_t_grid) - 1L)
  w <- (log_t - log_t_grid[j]) / (log_t_grid[j + 1L] - log_t_grid[j])
  cross <- function(col, th) {
    h <- cummax(cumhaz_grid[keep, col])
    i <- findInterval(th, h, left.open = TRUE) + 1L
    out <- rep(Inf, length(th))
    ok <- i <= length(tt)
    out[ok] <- tt[i[ok]]
    out
  }
  lo <- hi <- numeric(length(log_t))
  for (jj in unique(j)) {
    k <- which(j == jj)
    lo[k] <- cross(jj, threshold[k])
    hi[k] <- cross(jj + 1L, threshold[k])
  }
  tau <- (1 - w) * lo + w * hi
  # When only one neighbour crosses within the window, take the nearer one.
  one_side <- is.finite(lo) != is.finite(hi)
  tau[one_side] <- ifelse(w[one_side] < 0.5, lo[one_side], hi[one_side])
  tau
}

extinction <- function(n_cells, sigma, window, n_pop) {
  pop <- rep(seq_len(n_pop), each = n_cells)
  log_t <- log(500) + sigma * rnorm(n_cells * n_pop)
  tau <- death_times(log_t, -log(runif(n_cells * n_pop)), window)
  as.numeric(tapply(tau, pop, max))
}

set.seed(20260101)
ext_h <- extinction(100, 0, 56 * 24, 1000)
ext_pkpd <- extinction(100, sigma_t, 56 * 24, 1000)
```

Model PK (each cell has its own concentration but every cell experiences the
death rate averaged over the cells still alive) is not a per-cell model, so it
is not part of the packaged model. It is reproduced here from the per-cell
hazards for 200 populations: at each time step the alive cells' hazards are
averaged and that average is added to every alive cell's cumulative hazard.

```{r model-pk}
model_pk_extinction <- function(n_cells, sigma, window, n_pop) {
  keep <- which(tgrid <= window)
  vapply(seq_len(n_pop), function(p) {
    log_t <- log(500) + sigma * rnorm(n_cells)
    j <- pmin(pmax(findInterval(log_t, log_t_grid), 1L), length(log_t_grid) - 1L)
    w <- (log_t - log_t_grid[j]) / (log_t_grid[j + 1L] - log_t_grid[j])
    hz <- sweep(hazard_grid[keep, j, drop = FALSE], 2, 1 - w, `*`) +
      sweep(hazard_grid[keep, j + 1L, drop = FALSE], 2, w, `*`)
    threshold <- -log(runif(n_cells))
    h <- numeric(n_cells)
    alive <- rep(TRUE, n_cells)
    for (m in seq_along(keep)[-1]) {
      mu_avg <- mean(hz[m - 1L, alive])
      h[alive] <- h[alive] + mu_avg * dt / 24
      alive <- alive & h < threshold
      if (!any(alive)) {
        return(tgrid[keep[m]])
      }
    }
    Inf
  }, numeric(1))
}
ext_pk <- model_pk_extinction(100, sigma_t, 56 * 24, 200)
```


```{r table-1-check}
pkpd_extinct_pct <- 100 * mean(is.finite(ext_pkpd))
med_h <- median(ext_h)
med_pkpd <- median(ext_pkpd[is.finite(ext_pkpd)])
c(pkpd_extinct_pct = pkpd_extinct_pct, med_h = med_h, med_pkpd = med_pkpd)
stopifnot(
  # Every homogeneous population goes extinct (paper: 1000/1000)
  mean(is.finite(ext_h)) > 0.99,
  # Paper 63.6%; binomial SE with 1000 populations is 1.5 points
  abs(pkpd_extinct_pct - 63.6) < 10,
  # Paper medians 261 h (H) and 875 h (PKPD)
  abs(med_h / 261 - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(med_pkpd / 875 - 1) < 0.1,
  # Heterogeneity prolongs extinction by roughly 3.4-fold (paper)
  med_pkpd / med_h > 2.5
)
```

# Mean-field models (Experiment 3, Table 2, Figure 4)

The mean-field variants solve `dN/dt = -mu(C(t)) N` from `N(0) = 100` with a
single transporter count and call the population extinct when `N < 1`, i.e.
when the cumulative hazard reaches `log(100)`. The paper writes
`C(t) = kappa * T * C_p,u(t)` (QSS); both the QSS and the packaged ODE
concentration are shown.

```{r mean-field}
mf_time <- function(t_count, use_qss) {
  if (use_qss) {
    c_i <- kappa * t_count * typ$Cu
    mu <- 1.5 * c_i^2.5 / (2^2.5 + c_i^2.5)
    h <- c(0, cumsum((mu[-1] + mu[-length(mu)]) / 2 * dt / 24))
  } else {
    lt <- log(t_count)
    j <- findInterval(lt, log_t_grid)
    w <- (lt - log_t_grid[j]) / (log_t_grid[j + 1] - log_t_grid[j])
    h <- (1 - w) * cumhaz_grid[, j] + w * cumhaz_grid[, j + 1]
  }
  tgrid[which(h >= log(100))[1]]
}
mf <- data.frame(
  Variant = c("MF-mean", "MF-median", "MF-mode"),
  Transporters = c(660, 500, 379),
  Paper = c(216, 248, 346)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `QSS (h)` = vapply(Transporters, mf_time, numeric(1), use_qss = TRUE),
    `ODE (h)` = vapply(Transporters, mf_time, numeric(1), use_qss = FALSE)
  )
mf |>
  dplyr::rename("Paper (h)" = Paper) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Mean-field extinction times. Replicates Table 2.")
# Deterministic. Measured: MF-median 248.5 vs 248 h, MF-mode 362.5 vs 346 h
# (+5%). MF-mean comes out 184 vs 216 h (-15%) and is reported, not gated
# (see Assumptions and deviations).
stopifnot(
  abs(mf$`QSS (h)`[mf$Variant == "MF-median"] / 248 - 1) < 0.02,
  abs(mf$`QSS (h)`[mf$Variant == "MF-mode"] / 346 - 1) < 0.1,
  # All mean-field times sit far below the stochastic PKPD median (875 h)
  all(mf$`QSS (h)` < 0.5 * med_pkpd)
)
```

```{r figure-4, fig.cap = "Model PKPD extinction-time distribution (56-day window, extinct populations) with the mean-field predictions (QSS) as vertical lines. Replicates Figure 4."}
ggplot(data.frame(tau = ext_pkpd[is.finite(ext_pkpd)]), aes(tau)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 50, fill = "grey70", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(data = mf, aes(xintercept = `QSS (h)`, colour = Variant)) +
  labs(x = "Extinction time (h)", y = "Populations", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Population size (Experiment 4, Table S2)

200 populations per size over 180 days. Four of the paper's eight sizes are
reproduced to keep the article quick to build.

```{r scaling}
set.seed(20260103)
sizes <- c(100, 500, 1000, 2000)
scaling <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(sizes, function(n_cells) {
  e_h <- extinction(n_cells, 0, 180 * 24, 200)
  e_p <- extinction(n_cells, sigma_t, 180 * 24, 200)
  data.frame(
    N = n_cells,
    h_median_day = median(e_h) / 24,
    pkpd_failure_pct = 100 * mean(!is.finite(e_p)),
    pkpd_median_day = median(e_p[is.finite(e_p)]) / 24
  )
}))
paper_s2 <- data.frame(
  N = c(100, 500, 1000, 2000),
  paper_h_median_day = c(11.0, 13.8, 14.6, 16.0),
  paper_pkpd_failure_pct = c(2.5, 12.5, 24.5, 45.0),
  paper_pkpd_median_day = c(43.4, 91.6, 118.5, 133.0)
)
s2 <- dplyr::left_join(paper_s2, scaling, by = "N")
s2 |>
  dplyr::select(N, paper_h_median_day, h_median_day, paper_pkpd_failure_pct, pkpd_failure_pct, paper_pkpd_median_day, pkpd_median_day) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "H median, paper (day)" = paper_h_median_day, "H median, sim (day)" = h_median_day,
    "PKPD failure, paper (%)" = paper_pkpd_failure_pct, "PKPD failure, sim (%)" = pkpd_failure_pct,
    "PKPD median, paper (day)" = paper_pkpd_median_day, "PKPD median, sim (day)" = pkpd_median_day
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Extinction outcome vs. tumour cell count. Replicates Tables S2a and S2b.")
stopifnot(
  abs(median(s2$h_median_day / s2$paper_h_median_day - 1)) < 0.1,
  abs(median(s2$pkpd_median_day / s2$paper_pkpd_median_day - 1)) < 0.15,
  # Failure rises with population size (paper: 2.5% at N = 100, 45% at N = 2000)
  s2$pkpd_failure_pct[s2$N == 2000] - s2$pkpd_failure_pct[s2$N == 100] > 25
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Diffusion term omitted.** The paper's intracellular SDE has a diffusion
  coefficient `sigma_C = 0.01` (h^-1/2, on the concentration scale). rxode2
  integrates ODEs, so the packaged model carries the deterministic drift only.
  The stationary SD of that noise, `sigma_C / sqrt(2 k_met) = 0.022`, is about
  1% of EC50, and the paper's own Experiment 1 drops the noise (QSS). The
  extinction-time, mean-field and scaling results above are reproduced without
  it.
* **Concentration units.** The paper labels all concentrations uM, but its code
  computes the plasma concentration as dose (mg) / V/F (L) with no
  molecular-weight conversion (`pk.jl`; the free peak of about 0.01 and the
  calibration `0.38 * 500 * 0.0105 = 2.0 = EC50` both hold only on that
  scale). The packaged model keeps that numerical scale and labels it mg/L.
  The authors' code also carries stale reference values in its PK validation
  routine (steady-state Cmax 0.51, free Cmax 0.026, accumulation 2.4) that
  disagree with the paper text; the paper text is followed.
* **Transporter heterogeneity as a random effect.** `T_i` enters only through
  the product `k_in * T_i`, so it is encoded as a log-normal random effect on
  `kin_int_tumor` (geometric mean `0.038 * 500`, variance 0.25). Model H is
  `zeroRe()` of this model. Model PK, which averages death rates across cells,
  is a population-level construction and is reproduced in this article rather
  than in the model file.
* **sigma_T.** The paper uses `sigma_T = 0.5` (CV 53%) for all baseline
  experiments. Its Parameter Justification section also writes
  `sigma_T = sqrt(log(CV^2 + 1)) = 0.472 for CV = 53%`, which is the value for
  CV = 50%; 0.5 is used, as in the experiments and the code. The CV-indexed
  sensitivity tables (Table S3) convert CV to sigma_T with that formula, as done
  above.
* **Death-time resolution and integration.** The authors integrate with
  Euler-Maruyama at 0.1 h and update the hazard by the trapezoidal rule; here
  the ODE is integrated by LSODA and death is detected on a 0.5 h output grid.
  Monte Carlo draws differ from the paper's, so quantiles agree to within
  Monte Carlo and multimodality effects: the PKPD distribution is
  cycle-structured, so its lower quartile falls in a gap between treatment
  cycles and moves more than the median between runs. The 56-day PKPD
  extinction fraction comes out near 60% against the published 63.6% (about
  two to three binomial standard errors with 1000 populations), and the
  homogeneous lower quantiles are about 15% later than Table 1; the omitted
  diffusion term and the Euler step are the likely sources. Medians, upper
  quantiles, variances and the 180-day summaries agree to within about 5%.
* **Amplification factor.** The quadrature value at baseline (1.45e-6) is
  5% below the 1.525e-6 quoted for the 180-day runs and inside the
  1.445e-6 to 1.536e-6 range of replicate means in Table S2c.
* **Mean-field variants.** With the QSS concentration the paper writes, the
  MF-median extinction time reproduces Table 2 (248.5 vs. 248 h) and MF-mode
  is 5% above it (362.5 vs. 346 h), but MF-mean (660 transporters) comes out
  about 15% earlier than the published 216 h. The paper does not give enough
  detail to explain the MF-mean value; it is shown, not gated. The full ODE
  gives the slower values in the last column because intracellular
  concentrations lag plasma. The qualitative conclusion (all mean-field
  predictions fall far below the stochastic median) holds either way.
* **No residual error.** The model is a forward simulation of a mechanistic
  hypothesis; it has no observation model.
